text:
michael: Heads up — multiple multinode training jobs in us-west-2 started failing with NCCL connection timeouts after last night's kernel upgrade on gpu-k8s nodes. Error: "NCCL WARN TCP : Connection timed out", and some `failed to open qp` in the logs. Anyone seen this pattern?

josh: ugh. Any packet drops/ICMP 'fragmentation needed' in the dmesg or network stats? :thinking_face:

michael: checking; netstat -s shows a spike in ICMP messages. here's a quick dump:
```
$ ip -s link show bond0
4: bond0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped overrun mcast
    123456789  9876543 0       1024    0       0
    TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped carrier collsns
    987654321  8765432 0       3       0       0
$ netstat -s | grep -i icmp
    2300 ICMP messages received
    180 'destination unreachable' (frag needed)
```

tara: frag needed == PMTU issue. Are we running RoCEv2 over L3 with VXLAN overlays? VXLAN MTU + host MTU mismatch can cause UDP encaps packets to be too big and get ICMP frag-needed back to sender which breaks RoCE.

michael: we do have VXLAN for k8s overlay (flannel) and bond0 MTU is 1500. infra team ran a ToR config drift last night though.

sergio: can you check ibv_devinfo and ethtool offloads? I vaguely remember a kernel bump enabling GRO/GSO by default on our bonded interfaces that broke UDP-encap RDMA handshakes on some kernels.

michael: ran those:
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
    transport:                      InfiniBand (0)
    fw_ver:                         16.32.2030
    node_guid:                      0x248a07fffe123456
    sys_image_guid:                 0x248a07fffe654321
    max_mr_size:                    0xffffffffff
    vendor_id:                      0x02c9
    vendor_part_id:                 41212

$ ethtool -k bond0
Features for bond0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
```

josh: aha — `generic-receive-offload`/GRO can coalesce UDP packets and confuse upper layers for encapsulated RDMA. Try disabling GRO/GSO on the bond and underlying phys: `ethtool -K bond0 gso off gro off lro off` and same for eth0/eth1.

michael: did that on a suspect node and restarted the training job. immediate improvement — NCCL handshakes succeeded and no more "frag needed" ICMP in netstat. :tada:

tara: nice. That matches. We should treat this as a regression introduced by the kernel default and our overlay combination. Actions:
- pin offloads in cloud-init for GPU nodes
- add an e2e canary that runs an NCCL allreduce across 2 nodes after kernel/driver changes
- open ticket with infra provider/TOR team to reconcile MTU and ensure VXLAN path supports jumbo frames

sergio: also add a health-check that scans `ethtool -k` and flags `gso/gro` enabled on hosts running RoCE workloads.

michael: I'll push a tiny init script to /etc/network/if-pre-up.d/ to force offloads off for now and roll to us-west-2 pool. created PR 4321.

infra-bot: Deploy started: PR 4321 -> cluster/gpu/nodes (canary 1 -> 5 -> 50%)

josh: once canary is good, let's schedule a rolling fix. Also capture packettrace around UDP/4791 to double-check no fragmentation: `tcpdump -n -i bond0 -s0 -w /tmp/roach.pcap udp port 4791`.

michael: saved pcap from earlier; it shows large UDP payloads with DF set getting ICMP frag-needed back from ToR. attaching to the ticket.

tara: good root cause. Follow-up: add a short note to runbook about kernel offload defaults affecting RoCEv2 over overlays.

sergio: thanks all. closing once rollout finishes and canary passes. :white_check_mark:

michael: update — canary passed, rolling out to all us-west-2 GPU pools. Will watch metrics. Thanks everyone!
